summary: The control case ran (CheckRun 7224dba1ed234879b0cb1c65e5161bf7, exit 0) and behaved as a control should: with the target still holding its vote, the same public call moved leadership to the named server - target_ever_leader=true, the target the only leader seen and in Leader state at the end, the original leader in Follower and never leading again - with the term advancing by exactly one, from 2 to 3. Set against the vote-less case (CheckRun 2b61659461634c04b53ec61c35541227: target_suffrage=Nonvoter, target_ever_leader=false, term 2 to 4), the pair removes the alternative that the explicit transfer path is simply inoperative in this harness and makes the cost contrast concrete: the vote-less attempt advanced the term by two (the transfer campaign plus the re-election that recovered leadership) while moving authority nowhere. It also corrects my own earlier emphasis, which I have narrowed in the record: an empty transfer error cannot be the distinguishing signal, because the successful control reports the same empty value; what discriminates is who led and how the term moved. I recorded the control observation as a fact, wrote one interpretation that links both receipts with joint_history explaining they are same-shape separate executions differing in exactly one input (the target's suffrage, and in the vote-less run also the caller's prior demotion), and kept three counterweights and three limits - most importantly that a pair of separate runs does not exclude timing variation, and that neither case was repeated for its target type. To close that last gap I queued a repeat of the vote-less experiment, whose purpose is to see whether the non-transfer and its two-step term cost recur under a fresh schedule. Earlier witnessed findings on the configuration index and on duties lost at shutdown remain recorded and are unaffected by this turn.
